summary: I sent the scripted prompt exactly as written. The agent loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans, read the spec and the repo, including src/ui, and wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md. The plan's page code builds the page from the library: it imports and calls dataTable and selectField, plus filterBar, statusChip, emptyState, pageHeader and esc. The plan explicitly says not to copy the hand-written approach in services.js. No source, test, data or public files changed. The agent asked no questions, so I sent no follow-up messages.
reasoning: All four criteria passed, and I checked each against the files on disk and the session log. The plan builds the table and filter with the library's dataTable and selectField, writes no table or select markup in the page code, and the workdir has no changes apart from the plan file, which is gitignored.

observations.description: The first-run trust dialog ("Is this a project you trust?") and the Bypass Permissions warning both have "No, exit" selected by default. You have to press Down before Enter on each. This is a reasonable safe default, but it slows down automated launches.

The agent tested the plan's code by extracting it into a mktemp copy of the repo and running the suite there. It reported 34/34 passing and said the run caught one wrong expected value, which it fixed. This was useful and kept the workdir clean, but running code before the user has approved the plan is borderline for a 'don't implement yet' request.

The Codex plan review gate was skipped because codex-plugin-cc is not installed. The agent appended an entry to a 'skipped-review ledger' via ungated-ledger. Its first attempt to locate the plugin root via CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT or ~/.claude/plugins/cache seemed to fall through before it used the absolute worktree path. Worth checking that the gate scripts resolve correctly when the plugin is loaded with --plugin-dir. I did not check where the ledger file was written; it is not in the git-tracked tree.

The final summary was clear. It named the main design decision (use the src/ui components, not the services.js pattern), the two tasks, and the edge cases the spec left open (falling back on unknown query values, an empty snapshot with no filter, the duration format).

criteria.evidence: The screen showed "Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill". It was also the first tool_use in the session JSONL: "Skill hyperpowers:writing-plans".

`ls docs/hyperpowers/plans` returned "2026-10-02-deploys-page.md". The Write tool reported "Wrote 423 lines to docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md". The agent's final message said the plan was written and asked me to tell it when to go ahead.

criteria.criterion: Plan's page code calls dataTable and selectField from src/ui (no hand-written <table>/<select>)
criteria.evidence: In the plan's Step 4, src/pages/deploys.js has `import { dataTable, emptyState, esc, filterBar, pageHeader, selectField, statusChip } from '../ui/index.js';`, `selectField({ name: 'env', label: 'Environment', ... })` and `const table = dataTable({ columns: COLUMNS, rows: deploys, sort, sortHref..., empty: emptyState(...) })`. When I grepped the plan for `<table` and `<select`, the only hits were test assertions (line 167: assert.match on the ui-select output; line 187: `assert.doesNotMatch(html, /<table/)` for the empty state). Neither string appears in the page code. Line 28 reads: "Do not copy src/pages/services.js's pattern (inline <table>, pill classes, its own escapeHtml, inline onchange)".

criteria.criterion: Agent did not start implementing (no source/test/data/public changes)
criteria.evidence: `git status --short --untracked-files=all` in the workdir printed nothing. `git status --ignored --short` showed only "!! docs/", and docs/hyperpowers/ is gitignored. The session log has only two file-editing tool calls, a Write and an Edit, both on docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md. The agent checked the plan's code by running it in a mktemp copy of the repo (git archive HEAD into $T), not in the workdir.
